public_rationale: Read plainly, 'aren't going away anytime soon' means hallucinations would still be a material problem for at least about a year after May 2025. They were. In September 2025, OpenAI researchers wrote that hallucinations 'persist even in state-of-the-art systems.' In May 2026, a replication study found that frontier models released through March 2026 still invented nonexistent software packages 4.6–6.1% of the time. Labs did report real progress: OpenAI says GPT-5 made 'significant advances in reducing hallucinations.' But progress is not the same as the problem going away. Court cases involving hallucinated citations also kept accumulating through 2026.
limitations: The one-year window is the evaluator's reading of 'anytime soon'.
Reductions in some benchmarks might lead some readers to call the problem largely solved for certain tasks.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM hallucinations persist and will not go away anytime soon.

statement.excerpt: Bullshit. Hallucinations are still here, and aren’t going away, anytime soon.
statement.document_title: AI literacy, hallucinations, and the law: A case study

our_interpretation: The forecast is that LLM hallucinations will not be eliminated or become negligible in the near term.
'Anytime soon' has no stated date. Read plainly as at least about a year, so the window is set from the post date (2025-05-24) to 2026-05-24.
'Going away' means frontier LLMs no longer hallucinate at material rates on standard evaluations and in real use. Lower rates alone do not count as going away.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from within the window shows frontier LLMs still hallucinating at material rates, or researchers and labs describing hallucinations as persisting.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence from within the window shows frontier LLMs with negligible hallucination rates across standard evaluations and real use, or a credible demonstration that the problem has been eliminated.

evidence.excerpt: we measure overall hallucination rates between 4.62% (Claude Haiku 4.5) and 6.10% (GPT-5.4-mini) -- an order-of-magnitude compression of the inter-model spread observed by Spracklen, but not a retirement of the threat.
evidence.explanation: A May 2026 measurement found that frontier models released up to March 2026 still invented nonexistent software packages about 5–6% of the time. Hallucinations had not gone away by the end of the window.
